The Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, is dead. Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital after a brief illness, the management of Vanguard Media Limited has announced. In a Monday statement signed by the Editor of Vanguard, Eze Anaba, the management described his death as a massive loss to the organisation and the journalism profession. “His death is a massive loss to the Vanguard family and the journalism profession,” the statement said. The management said the 44-year-old Ajasa was a valued member of the organisation who made significant contributions to the growth of its digital operations and online journalism. Add us to your Preferred Sources Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido, in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University between 2004 and 2009. He also obtained a certification in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, in 2015. Ajasa began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013. He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, serving until September 2016. He subsequently moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked from 2016 to 2021, first as Online Editor and later as Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations. In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager before returning to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death. The management said Ajasa’s return to the organisation marked the continuation of a relationship that began early in his professional career. It expressed condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and members of the Vanguard family. “The management of Vanguard Media Limited deeply regrets this irreparable loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and all members of the Vanguard family,” the statement said. The statement added that the organisation’s thoughts and prayers were with his family, expressing hope that God would grant them the strength and fortitude to bear the loss. The Service of Songs/Wake-Keep in his honour will hold at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos, on Thursday, November 19, at 5 pm. Other funeral arrangements will be announced by the family.
